clue.text: Everyone says scab can't — you'll have to work

definitions.note: a phrase meaning 'according to what everyone says'

indicators.note: the letters are made to work, put through their paces until they form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A striker's taunt at a strikebreaker: you can't scab now, you'll have to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have to work' tells you to rearrange SCAB, CANT and YOULL, thirteen letters that give the phrase. A scab is a worker who crosses a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock idiom for reported general opinion: according to every report going round.

clue.text: Hippy resolves to be a bit hard on me

indicators.note: to resolve is to break into parts and recombine, so the letters are rearranged

parts.words: be a bit hard on me

explanation.surface: A hippie decides to go a little hard on the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippy' looks like a flower child; it means wide-hipped. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with broad hips is described with this nautical idiom for a ship wide across its middle.

clue.text: Detectives take it up as an aid to detection

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the UK police detective branch
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Police detectives taking a case up as a tool for detection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole of CID plus SA, giving the letters backwards; 'take' and 'as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British name for early sonar, a device for detecting submarines.

clue.text: To induce error, relays data in garbled form

indicators.note: garbled data is jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Corrupted transmission of data leads people into mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone, steering them into a mistake or wrongdoing, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Reticent about information given to head of CID — it could produce conviction

indicators.note: the shy word goes around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: coy means reticent, shy
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped informant passes facts to the CID chief, which may secure a guilty verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests a court case, but here it means being convinced.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasive force in an argument is what brings a listener to firm belief.

clue.text: Insult not in vogue

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the current fashion

explanation.surface: An insult that is no longer fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A gross affront or offence is the noun's sense, as in an outrage against decency.

clue.text: The devil can

explanation.surface: A claim that the devil is capable of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a nickname for Satan, and in British slang both words mean jail.

clue.text: Suspect foul play when the fish eat Tennyson's headless lady

indicators.note: the fish swallows the lady, so she goes inside it

parts.note: a smelt is a small fish

indicators.note: her first letter is cut off

parts.note: Lady Clara Vere de Vere is the subject of a Tennyson poem

explanation.surface: Suspicion arises when fish devour a decapitated Tennyson heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennyson's' points to his poem Lady Clara Vere de Vere; her name loses its head to give LARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense that something is wrong or that someone is cheating.

clue.text: Conservatives make a bloomer with historic measure

parts.note: a primrose is a flower, something that blooms
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: Tory politicians make a blunder with an old piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is a flower. The answer was a Victorian society promoting Conservative principles.
explanation.definitionFit: This organisation, founded in 1883 in Disraeli's memory, spread Tory values, so its members were Conservatives.

clue.text: Concerning a piece from a cask

parts.note: on can mean about or concerning, as in a talk on art
a draught is a playing piece in the board game draughts (checkers)

explanation.surface: Talking about a piece of something taken out of a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; each counter is a draught.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer served straight from the barrel rather than bottled is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Sure about king

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A confident statement concerning a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being certain of something is to be in no doubt, plain in one's mind; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Us prosecutor takes tea in Russian country house

parts.note: a DA, District Attorney, is an American public prosecutor
cha (char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: An American lawyer drinks tea at a Russian rural retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is the word for a second home or villa in the Russian countryside.

clue.text: Protection against birds put round a spruce

indicators.note: the netting is placed around the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a net is draped over fruit to keep birds off

explanation.surface: Netting placed around a fir tree to keep birds away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' looks like the tree, but here it is the adjective meaning smart and tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone smart and trim in appearance, tidy and well turned out.

clue.text: Overcrowded buildings, fifty in total

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the singular answer names a district of such buildings

indicators.note: the Roman fifty sits inside the word for a total

parts.note: a sum is a total
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A count showing fifty overcrowded blocks altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of squalid, crowded housing is the noun's sense; the clue describes what fills it.

clue.text: Oldest inhabitant negotiated oil bargain

indicators.note: a deal that is negotiated is worked over and reshaped, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A native elder strikes a deal over oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An original, first-known native of a land is its earliest occupant.

clue.text: At regular intervals, chivalrous king disappears

indicators.note: the king's letter vanishes from the adjective, leaving the rest

parts.note: knightly means chivalrous, like a knight
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A courtly monarch keeps vanishing at set times.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every evening happens on a regular cycle, once per day after dark.

clue.text: Bird or heraldic device

explanation.surface: A choice between a bird and a coat-of-arms emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny songbird has a golden stripe on its head, and in heraldry a crest in gold is a gilt emblem above a shield.

clue.text: Hence trammelling doctor with a prohibition

indicators.note: to trammel is to hem in or confine, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, hence
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Therefore a physician is restricted by a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade with a country is the standard meaning: a formal prohibition.

clue.text: A line from Henry to the court

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a yard is a courtyard

explanation.surface: A message sent by Henry to the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' looks like a line of writing from Henry, but it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship this rope raises or lowers a sail, so it is a kind of line.

clue.text: Should be under the doctor when it doesn't rain

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: ought means should

explanation.surface: Someone ought to be under medical care during dry weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without rainfall is a dry period, the time when the skies stay clear.

clue.text: Sort out target, zero in and finish off

indicators.note: sorting out the letters puts them into a new order

parts.note: zero is O, the round figure

explanation.surface: Instructions for a sniper: identify the target, home in, then kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zero in' looks like aiming, but zero is just O, mixed with TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle someone with a cord or wire is to kill them, a grim way to finish a victim.

clue.text: Pulpit covered with scrambled egg — it's yellow

indicators.note: the pulpit is wrapped by the egg letters, enclosed by them
scrambled egg is mixed up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: an ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early churches

explanation.surface: A church pulpit smeared with scrambled egg turns a yellowish colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' mixes the egg into letters that split around the pulpit; an ambo is an old church term few solvers know. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This gum resin from Asian trees gives a deep golden pigment used by painters.

clue.text: Burn a summons

explanation.surface: A notice to appear in court is set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn in Scotland and a beck in northern England are both a mountain stream; a beck is also a beckoning gesture, as in 'at someone's beck and call'.

clue.text: One who wrote many a verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was a writer
M, the Roman thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: A prolific author who wrote a lot of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of verse is a composition in lines and metre, the same thing as the answer.

clue.text: It sounds big to have to reduce to little bits

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for big is heard, not spelt

parts.note: great means big

explanation.surface: Something that sounds impressive gets chopped down to size.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing cheese against a grater shreds it into small pieces, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Like a Scotsman or an Indian

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: Resembling either a Scot or someone from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from India is a native of that continent, east of Europe.

clue.text: Second player

explanation.surface: The runner-up competitor in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it, and in football or rugby a defender is a full-back or half-back.

clue.text: Space in which the culmination of the action occurs

definitions.text: Space in which the culmination of the action occurs

parts.words: Space in which the culmination of the action occurs
parts.note: a ring or stadium where combat or sport is played out; the closing letter of the word action also ends this space's name

explanation.surface: A stage where a drama reaches its climax.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports ground or amphitheatre is the place where contests are fought out.

clue.text: Getting down to earth, basic instruction

explanation.surface: Practical first lessons that bring a student down to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing a plane or running aground is taking it to earth, and a thorough training in fundamentals is also called this.

clue.text: Cross the Rubicon, or jump in?

explanation.surface: A question of whether to commit or to dive into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossing the Rubicon is the classic irrevocable decision, an idiom for committing boldly, and literally it means to dive into water.
